oneLineCopy: Invoices out, numbers straight — no spreadsheet, no gut feeling.

hero.headlineMain: Your numbers, honest at any hour.
hero.headlineSerifLead: Write invoices, track payments, see liquidity — and know how long your money actually lasts.

founderScenario.story: Daniel opens his banking app for the third time this week, adds up the open invoices in his head and weighs them against rent. The answer to "is this enough?" sits somewhere between two accounts and a spreadsheet from last quarter. He closes the window again without it.

benefits: You no longer write invoices — you approve them
You can see at any moment what comes in, what goes out and what stays
Open items chase themselves before they go stale
Liquidity forecast: how long your money lasts, without a spreadsheet
The numbers come from your real receipts, not from your memory
howSteps: Your receipts and bank movements already run through your Aven
finance brain turns them into receivables, payables and tomorrow's balance
Invoices are drafted from an offer or delivery — you check and release
Open items get tracked and chased without you keeping a list

whatMechanics.input: Receipts from docs organizer, bookings from book keeper, bank movements and your offers
whatMechanics.magic: Invoice drafting → payment matching → open-item tracking → liquidity forecast
whatMechanics.output: Invoices ready for release · an honest finance dashboard · a forecast of how long it lasts

playsWith.relation: Was gebucht ist, ist auch im Dashboard richtig
Belege liefern die Zahlen, ohne Abtippen
Keine Rechnung geht raus, die du nicht freigegeben hast
Eingehende Rechnungen landen direkt im richtigen Vorgang

valueStack.timeDelayToValue: The first dashboard stands once your receipts have run through
valueStack.effortToInstall: Connect the account — the receipts are already there
valueStack.proof: Still in the workshop: finance brain runs on our own numbers before it runs on yours.

bonuses: Reminder stages that start politely and still work
Tax reserve: what to set aside before you spend it
Month-end in one view instead of seven tabs
letterFromPublisher: The most dangerous number in a founder's life is the one he only estimates. Daniel estimated for months — and was narrowly wrong every time, always in the same direction. I'm building the thing that takes that off him: a number that holds, even when it's uncomfortable.
